enquiry: We want to monitor water content in a clear ethanol-water stream in our solvent recovery unit. Water content is between 0.5 and 5 % w/w, the line runs at 25 °C in a DN50 stainless steel pipe, and the analyzer can sit in a control room about 20 m away. Our reference is Karl Fischer titration in the lab, and we need an updated value every minute.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when water content is not known in real time, and which operating decision should the minute-by-minute value drive?
clarification_questions.why: Identifies the decision the monitor serves, which sets the required accuracy and whether the value feeds control or only monitoring.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Monitoring only, with the lab Karl Fischer value as the reference; no control loop assumed.

clarification_questions.question: Besides ethanol and water, what other components or impurities are in the stream, and how much do they vary?
clarification_questions.why: Other components can interfere with the optical signal and make a calibration valid only for one composition.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Stream is treated as ethanol-water only; the calibration must be checked against real samples in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: What are the line pressure and the fouling or cleaning conditions of the DN50 pipe, and does the stream contain bubbles or particles?
clarification_questions.why: Pressure, deposits, cleaning chemicals and gas bubbles determine probe design, materials and the robustness of the measurement.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pressure unknown; no fouling or bubbles assumed, to be confirmed in an in-line trial.

clarification_questions.question: Where exactly can a probe be installed on the DN50 line, and is there an existing port or fitting for it?
clarification_questions.why: The available port and whether the probe can be in contact with the flow determine the probe geometry and the installation effort.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: A suitable port exists in the DN50 line; probe geometry to be decided after the site visit.

clarification_questions.question: Is there any existing optical fiber between the line and the control room, and what is its type and length?
clarification_questions.why: The fiber type limits which spectral range can reach the analyzer, and the 20 m separation affects the choice of fiber and analyzer location.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No existing fiber; a suitable fiber link for the 20 m separation is to be checked against the spectral range needed.

clarification_questions.question: What is the accuracy and sampling frequency of the current Karl Fischer reference, and how often are reference samples taken from the line?
clarification_questions.why: The Karl Fischer data are the basis for calibration and validation; their accuracy sets the achievable accuracy of the monitor.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference accuracy unknown; the monitor cannot be judged better than the reference until this is known.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy is required over the 0.5 to 5 % w/w range, and what response time is needed beyond the one-minute update?
clarification_questions.why: Accuracy and response time decide whether a simple few-wavelength sensor or a broader analyzer is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Accuracy and response time unknown; the one-minute update is the only stated requirement.

clarification_questions.question: What is the budget and the timeline for a feasibility trial, including whether an in-line trial in the real line is possible?
clarification_questions.why: Budget and trial access determine how many lab and in-line steps can be run before a sensor is chosen.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Budget unknown; the feasibility plan starts with lab screening on representative samples, followed by an in-line trial if access is granted.

flags_before_revision.detail: shortlisted row not screened: Raman spectroscopy / Raman probe

different_context: The source states NIR transmission is preferred for transparent or semi-transparent liquids in the context of dairy/milk analysis (skim milk, whey, permeate), not as a general rule for clear liquids such as ethanol-water; the claim transfers it without saying so. Fix: State that the source example is dairy (milk, whey) and that NIR transmission for clear liquids is inferred, not confirmed for this ethanol-water sample.

not_supported: S01 p.16 and S02 p.6 do not state that mid-IR needs chalcogenide or polycrystalline fibers for this application; S02 p.6 lists fiber transmission ranges only and does not say water absorbs strongly in the IR as a reason for this choice in the cited pages. Fix: Cite the fiber transmission ranges from S02 p.6 and state the water absorption point only as a general expectation, or drop the unsupported water-absorption reasoning.

not_supported: The cited pages list fiber transmission ranges and a 100-300 m silica cable; they do not mention a 20 m control room link or state that silica suits NIR while mid-IR needs PIR or CIR as a link rule. Fix: Remove the 20 m link conclusion or attribute it to the project brief rather than the cited pages; state only the fiber ranges shown on S02 p.6.

overstated: S02 p.6 gives transmission ranges but does not define which fibers fully or partially cover NIR or MIR as a 'rule check'; the full/partial classification is the claim author's inference, presented as sourced fact. Fix: Present the full/partial coverage as an inference from the listed ranges, and note that exact values must be checked against the figure and the actual fiber configuration.

overstated: The cited page does not establish that the fiber family is undefined as a fact preventing any compatibility check; it only shows fiber ranges, so the statement that these prevent checking is more certain than the page supports. Fix: Say that the fiber family and link length are not yet defined, so compatibility should be checked before selecting components.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
